look: Munition: plain brown leather over wood, iron chape, belt tails laced round the throat; used
prompt: Museum catalogue photo of a single object: an empty medieval sword scabbard, 14th century, Baltic (Reval 1343), 84 cm long, plain munition grade issued to a town sergeant. Straight, flat oval section 6 cm wide at the mouth narrowing evenly to 3.5 cm at the tip, both sides mirror each other. Wooden core covered in plain brown vegetable-tanned leather with one stitched seam along the back; a simple plain iron chape 7 cm long at the tip, no locket at the mouth. Two narrow brown leather sword-belt tails, about 8 cm and 20 cm below the mouth, are laced tightly around the scabbard itself in a criss-cross wrap and cut off short, lying flat on its surface, nothing hanging. Used: leather scuffed and darkened, a few scratches on the chape. No ornament, no studs, no buckles, no frog, no baldric, no gold, not fantasy, no sword in it. Lying horizontally, mouth on the left and tip on the right, seen almost straight from above with a slight three-quarter tilt, whole object in frame with margin, plain pure white background, soft even studio light, no cast shadow, no hands, no people, no text.
